 The election is over, but our responsibility isn't 
 By Darrell Bramer 
 Nov 8, 2026 
 Nov 8, 2026 
 Updated 
 8 hrs ago

 As of this writing on Oct. 30, 2026, the election results have not been tallied, but I took advantage of early voting today. I truly consider it a privilege and am thankful for the opportunity. 
 While I've always voted, I feel like I've taken it for granted more than I should have. But as I've grown older, and hopefully wiser, I've come to appreciate how much of a privilege it really is. People around the world would give anything to walk into a voting booth and have a voice in their future. I'm thankful we live in a country where we have that right. 
 As another election comes to a close, some people will be celebrating, others will be disappointed and some will probably be wondering where we go from here. 
 I've always believed there's a path forward, regardless of election results. 
 Having spent nearly 60 years in Oldham County, I've seen a lot of changes: some good, some challenging and certainly some I didn't agree with. But through it all, I've continued to believe in this community and the people who call it home — and that belief doesn't change with an election. 
 My faith has taught me that God can’t be surprised. While I may not always understand why things happen the way they do, I find peace in knowing that he does. 
 That doesn't mean everything will be easy, or that we should sit back and accept things we don't agree with — far from it. 
 We should keep standing up for what we believe. We should keep having conversations, and yes, even with those who see things differently. We should keep getting involved in our community and be part of the solution, not adding to any division. Regardless of the election outcomes, we still have the ability and the responsibility to make a difference. 
 As this election comes to a close, we should also take a moment to thank those who put their names on the ballot, knowing they won't make everyone happy. 
 I appreciate public service. And I can tell you, it's not always pretty. I have experience in local government, volunteering in my community and in broader elections. The criticism, the personal attacks and the expectations can be exhausting, and it seems that in today's environment, public service is even more difficult. 
 So, to those who genuinely stepped forward to serve their community and make things better, thank you. I admire your willingness to put yourself out there. 
 We need good people who are willing to serve, even when it's difficult. 
 I would also be remiss if I didn't mention something else I hope we don't lose sight of, and it's probably what matters most to me: the next generation! 
 Our kids and grandkids are watching. They're watching how we respond when things don't go our way. They're watching how we talk about and talk with the people we disagree with. And they're absolutely learning from us, whether we realize it or not. 
 Our children and grandchildren won't remember every election result, but they will remember how we treated one another along the way. 
 So, when we think about the next generation, I hope we can have the right answers when we ask: 
 What are we teaching them when our candidate loses? 
 What are we showing them when our candidate wins? 
 Are we teaching them to be gracious, listen and stand firm in their beliefs while still respecting others, or are we teaching them that if someone disagrees with us, they're somehow the enemy? 
 I hope it's the former. We can and should disagree on politics and still care about one another. We can have strong convictions without tearing someone else down and we can be disappointed in an outcome without losing hope in the future. 
 As we move past this election, I hope we'll remember there's still good work to be done here in Oldham County, across Kentucky and throughout our country. 
 There are families who need support, young people who need encouragement, neighbors who need help and communities that need people willing to step up. 
 None of those needs change because of who won an election. 
 So, whether your candidates won or lost, I hope you'll stay involved. Keep standing up for your beliefs, keep serving others and keep fighting for the next generation. 
 At the end of the day, the future isn't shaped by elections alone. It's shaped by what each of us chooses to do in the days, months and years that follow. 
 For me, my faith tells me there's still plenty of reason to be hopeful.
